title: the push guard judges a push in the session's clone, not the clone it runs in
status: fixed after 0.5.0: the guard judges each push in the clone it runs in (DESIGN.md, 13)
world: memory; the git world runs it over real git (build step 6)

steps.note: b fetches in its second clone, b-other, makes a claim commit naming itself there, and runs git -C ../b-other push --force-with-lease origin claude/1 from its session's clone, which never fetched claude/1: git would take the lease from b-other, and the guard, judging the push in b-other, reads a's claim file on origin/claude/1 and b's on the branch pushed and refuses it; under the mutant that ignores git's and env's -C, which judges the push in the session's own clone, where no claim file shows on origin/claude/1, the fence cannot judge, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the same push by cd ../b-other && git push --force-with-lease origin claude/1: the guard follows the shell's cd into b-other and refuses it; under the mutant that does not follow the shell's moves the push is judged in the session's clone, taken, and G11a and G1 are red here

the same push by cd ../b-other; cd ../b-nowhere; git push --force-with-lease origin claude/1: the first cd is made and the second fails, since no clone b-nowhere is there, so the shell pushes from b-other, and the guard, judging the push where the shell stood, refuses it; under the mutant that takes a cd to what is not a directory as made, the push is judged in b-nowhere, which shows nothing, and where the command starts, in b's own clone, which never fetched claude/1, so the fence cannot judge, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

b fetches claude/1 in its own clone this time, makes a claim commit naming itself there, and runs the push after a here-document whose body holds cd ..: the shell reads the body as text and pushes from b's own clone, and the guard, which reads the body's cd as one the shell makes, judges the push also where the command starts, as if no cd ran, and refuses it there; under the mutant that judges a push only where the shell's moves take it, the push is judged in the directory that holds the clones, which shows nothing, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the same push by git -C "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)", which names b's own clone through a path the shell expands: the guard cannot tell the clone, so it judges the push by its words and in the session's own clone, and refuses it there; under the mutant that judges such a push by its words alone, the fence cannot judge, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here
